clue.text: Long-distance runner going from black forest to black sea

definitions.text: Long-distance runner going from black forest to black sea

parts.words: Long-distance runner going from black forest to black sea
parts.note: a runner here is a river, not an athlete; the course runs from the Black Forest in Germany to the Black Sea

explanation.surface: An endurance athlete jogs from a dark wood all the way to a dark ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Lower-case 'black forest' and 'black sea' hide the proper names: the Black Forest is in south-west Germany and the Black Sea lies beyond Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: This great European river rises in the Black Forest and flows into the Black Sea, a run of nearly three thousand kilometres.

clue.text: A heavy drop from the sky

definitions.text: A heavy drop from the sky

parts.words: A heavy drop from the sky
parts.note: reads like something falling or a plane plummeting, but means a heavy fall of rain

explanation.surface: Something weighty plunges down from above.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrential burst of rain is a heavy fall of water from the clouds.

clue.text: From Eden you start to be poverty-stricken

indicators.note: the letters are taken from the word Eden and made into a different word
the start of the word you is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Banished from paradise, you begin life in poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' signals that NEED is made from the letters of EDEN; 'you start' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in want, lacking the basic necessities, is what poor means.

clue.text: Pester one, sound disapproving with cause for anxiety

parts.note: to pester someone is to bug them
one is the indefinite article a
boo is the noise a crowd makes in disapproval

explanation.surface: Nagging someone and jeering at them gives them reason to worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear or object of dread is a source of worry.

clue.text: One-armed brigand?

parts.note: pictures a robber with only one arm, recalling the slang name for a slot machine with a single lever

explanation.surface: A highway robber who has lost an arm.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'one-armed bandit' is a fruit machine that swallows coins; a brigand is a robber, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is an outlaw or robber, and the slot machine is nicknamed after one.

clue.text: Generally free

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in general (the public at large) and also escaped or unconfined, as a prisoner on the run.

clue.text: Young woman with wideawake little creature

parts.note: a damsel is an old word for a young woman
fly is British slang for knowing or alert

explanation.surface: A girl who is very alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wideawake' is also a kind of felt hat, a distraction; FLY in the sense of sharp and streetwise is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: This slender insect, a relative of the dragonfly, is a small winged creature.

clue.text: Strive towards taking a stand

indicators.note: the words strive towards take in, or hold, the answer within them

explanation.surface: Struggle to adopt a position on an issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged metal support for a pot or kettle is a stand.

clue.text: Sword that cuts both ways

parts.note: describes a blade sharpened on each side, and also an argument or remark with effects for and against

explanation.surface: A blade sharpened on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-sided blade can cut in either direction, and figuratively something double-edged works against as well as for you.

clue.text: Having been deprived of spirit and confidence made soldier upset

definitions.text: Having been deprived of spirit and confidence

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something demoralising made a soldier distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges MADE SOLDIER into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Disheartened people have lost their morale, their fighting spirit and self-belief.

clue.text: It's clear, rascal has broken cover

indicators.note: the rascal has broken into the cover, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a lid is a cover
an imp is a mischievous rascal

explanation.surface: A naughty child has smashed the top of something, and it is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that is transparent and unclouded is limpid, as is lucid prose.

clue.text: Agent crosses eastern river in Scotland

indicators.note: the agent crosses, or straddles, the letter for eastern, which sits inside

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: A spy travels east over a Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: This salmon-fishing river flows through north-east Scotland into the Moray Firth.

clue.text: Short jacket from bottom cabinet

parts.note: bum is British slang for the bottom
a freezer is a cold storage cabinet

explanation.surface: A small coat taken out of the lowest cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The jacket is named because it stops at the waist, leaving the seat exposed to the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A bum-freezer is British slang for a waist-length coat, such as an Eton jacket.

clue.text: Clothes second person's ego? Do what you like

parts.note: a suit is a set of clothes
your is the second-person possessive
the ego is one's self

explanation.surface: Dressing one's own vanity is permitted: do as you please.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to please themselves, granting permission with indifference.

clue.text: Boiler found in the kitchen

parts.note: suggests a central-heating boiler, but means a vessel for heating water for a brew

explanation.surface: The heating appliance is located in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot for boiling water to make the drink is a kitchen boiler.

clue.text: Coated?

parts.note: coated suggests a layer of paint or sauce, but here means wearing a coat-like garment, or a potato in its skin

explanation.surface: Covered in something?
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing an outer garment, or covered in a skin as a baked potato is, means having a covering.

clue.text: Soldier unwell in channel by island

indicators.note: the word for unwell goes in the word for channel

parts.note: an artery is a channel, for blood or traffic
unwell means ill
Man is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A sick soldier in a waterway beside an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea; crosswords often clue it as 'island'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunner serving with the big guns is a kind of soldier.

clue.text: You have had your allotted span

definitions.text: You have had your allotted span

parts.words: You have had your allotted span
parts.note: sounds like a solemn word on mortality but is the call that ends a turn or a quiz round

explanation.surface: Your life has run its course.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase announces that the permitted period for a task is over.

clue.text: Cut tax on day one

parts.note: excise is a duty or tax on goods

indicators.note: day one is the first letter of the word day

explanation.surface: A tax reduction comes in on the first day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a tax cut, but it is the definition; 'day one' gives D, the first letter of day.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something out surgically or from a text is to remove it.

clue.text: The lady's as content finding female animal

indicators.note: the word as is the content, held inside the other piece

parts.note: the lady's contracts to she's, she is

explanation.surface: The woman is pleased at discovering a female beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A female donkey is a jenny, a female beast of burden.

clue.text: It is not bound to be played

definitions.text: It is not bound to be played

parts.words: It is not bound to be played
parts.note: seems to say something is under no obligation to be performed, but means printed music on loose pages, not in a bound volume

explanation.surface: Something is under no obligation to be performed.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose printed scores, not bound into a book, are what a pianist plays from.

clue.text: Edible soap?

parts.note: soap comes in a bar called by the same name as a baked treat, so the edible version is the sweet

explanation.surface: Soap that can be eaten?
explanation.definitionFit: A block of soap shares its name with the baked dessert, which is the version you can eat.

clue.text: Dog one going over a court

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single dog passes across a courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue CUR and I go over, that is above, A.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal court and administration in Rome, or an ancient Roman senate house, is a court.

clue.text: In dramatic act used spiny plant

indicators.note: the answer is found in the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: A prickly plant was used in a theatrical scene.
explanation.definitionFit: This desert succulent is covered in spines.

clue.text: Separate secret I'd unravelled

indicators.note: unravelled means untangled, so the letters are pulled apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hidden matter I had has come undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravelled' rearranges SECRET and ID. Don't confuse the answer with DISCREET, meaning tactful.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct and individually distinguishable things are separate from one another.

clue.text: Likely to drop off

parts.note: suggests something loose that might fall, but means about to nod off into slumber

explanation.surface: Something is liable to fall away.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drowsy, someone is ready to fall asleep.

clue.text: I had eccentric identification document

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
a card is an eccentric or amusing character

explanation.surface: I owned a peculiar passport.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass card carrying your name and photograph proves who you are.
